label: RITVAYA • BASICS
caption:
Ayurveda is often introduced as a list of remedies. A herb for this, a ritual for that. That's why it can feel confusing.

At its root, Ayurveda means "knowledge of life." The classical text Charaka Samhita states its purpose simply: first protect the health of the healthy, then treat illness.

Its framework is built on three doshas:
→ Vata: movement (breath, circulation, thought)
→ Pitta: transformation (digestion, metabolism)
→ Kapha: structure (stability, strength, lubrication)

Everyone has all three in a personal mix. Health, in this view, is keeping that mix in balance through daily rhythm: when you sleep, when and how you eat, and how you adjust with the seasons.

What modern research adds:
• Doshas are a traditional framework, not something measured in a lab.
• Regular sleep and meal timing line up with modern circadian research.
• Studies on some herbs, like turmeric and ashwagandha, are growing but mixed.
• Quality matters. A 2008 JAMA study found about 1 in 5 Ayurvedic products sold online contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic. Choose tested products and talk to your doctor before taking herbs.

So Ayurveda doesn't ask you to do more. It asks you to put what you already do in order.

Start with this today: pick one steady wake time and keep it for 3 days. Observe what changes.
